name: MSR Hubba Hubba 2
description: Freestanding two-person semi-geodesic. Two doors and two porches, so neither person climbs over the other. Pitches inner-first.

name: Terra Nova Laser Compact 2
description: Lightweight two-person tunnel tent with a single side entrance. Pitches as one, which is welcome in rain.

name: Wild Country Zephyros Compact 2
description: Sturdy budget two-person tunnel tent. Heavier fabric than race-weight shelters, and more tolerant of grit and wind for it.

name: Vango Nevis 200
description: Two-person semi-geodesic at an entry price. Snug for two adults but genuinely under 2kg.

name: Alpkit Soloist
description: One-person tunnel tent with a generous porch. A lot of shelter for the weight, if you are out alone.

name: Hilleberg Nallo 2
description: Four-season tunnel tent in Kerlon 1200. Built for sustained wind and snow loading rather than fair-weather weekends.

name: Robens Boulder 3
description: Roomy three-person dome with standing-ish headroom at the centre. Too heavy to carry far, excellent from a car boot.

name: Vango Tay 400
description: Four-berth family tunnel tent with a sewn-in groundsheet. Summer festival and campsite duty.

name: Rab Ascent 500
description: 650 fill-power down bag with a comfort limit around -3C. The dependable British three-season choice.

name: Mountain Equipment Glacier 450
description: Hydrophobic down, a touch warmer than most three-season bags. Suits people who sleep cold or camp late in the year.

name: Alpkit PipeDream 400
description: Light 750 fill-power down bag with a close-fitting cut. Excellent warmth for the weight if you do not mind a snug bag.

name: Sea to Summit Trek TkII
description: Roomier cut than most down bags, with a full side zip for venting on mild nights.

name: Vango Ultralite Pro 200
description: Synthetic summer bag. Cheap, forgiving of damp, and no use at all below freezing.

name: Rab Neutrino 800
description: 800 fill-power expedition down bag. Serious winter warmth, priced accordingly.

name: Therm-a-Rest NeoAir XLite NXT
description: Inflatable pad with an R-value of 4.5 at well under 400g. Crinkles audibly, which some people hate.

name: Therm-a-Rest ProLite
description: Self-inflating foam pad. Less plush than an air mat but far harder to puncture out of use.

name: Sea to Summit Ether Light XT Extreme
description: 10cm thick with an R-value over 6. The pad to pair with a winter bag, and good for side sleepers.

name: Alpkit Dozer
description: Budget self-inflating mat. Heavier than the alternatives, and a third of the price.

name: Jetboil Flash
description: Integrated canister system that boils half a litre in around 100 seconds. Boils water brilliantly; simmers poorly.

name: MSR PocketRocket 2
description: 73g screw-on canister burner. No integrated pot, so you choose your own, and it actually simmers.

name: Primus Lite Plus
description: Integrated system with a proper simmer control, so it cooks as well as it boils.

name: Trangia 27-1 UL
description: Meths burner in a windproof cookset. Slow and heavy, and nearly impossible to break.

name: Alpkit Kraku
description: 45g titanium burner. About as light as a stove gets, with a small pot support to match.

name: Osprey Atmos AG 65
description: Anti-Gravity suspended mesh back. Carries heavy loads unusually well, at the cost of 2kg empty.

name: Gregory Baltoro 75
description: Large-volume expedition pack with a rotating hipbelt. For multi-week trips or winter loads.

name: Lowe Alpine AirZone Trail 35
description: Ventilated daypack that stretches to an overnight. Sits in the gap between day walks and full backpacking.

name: Osprey Talon 22
description: Close-fitting daypack that moves with you rather than swinging. Day walks and fast hill days.

name: Alpkit Gourdon 30
description: Roll-top drybag pack. Fully waterproof, minimal back system, very light.

name: Petzl Actik Core
description: 600 lumens on a rechargeable core that swaps for AAAs when it dies mid-trip.

name: Black Diamond Spot 400
description: 400 lumens, IPX8 waterproof, with a lock mode so it does not drain in your pack.

name: Alpkit Viper
description: Light, cheap, rechargeable. Enough for camp chores and a path, not for route-finding off track.

name: Sawyer Squeeze
description: 0.1 micron hollow-fibre filter that threads onto a bottle. Needs backflushing, otherwise lasts for years.

name: Katadyn BeFree 1L
description: Collapsible soft flask with a fast-flowing filter. Fastest to drink from, shortest lifespan.

name: LifeStraw Peak Series Solo
description: Compact personal filter for topping up from streams on the move.

name: MSR Guardian Purifier
description: Self-cleaning pump purifier that removes viruses as well as bacteria. Overkill for UK streams.

name: Rab Microlight Alpine Jacket
description: 700 fill-power recycled down with a helmet-compatible hood. The default British hill down jacket.

name: Mountain Equipment Particle Hooded Jacket
description: Synthetic insulation that keeps working when damp. The safer choice for wet British trips.

name: Patagonia Nano Puff Hoody
description: Light synthetic midlayer that packs into its own pocket. Wind resistant, not especially warm.

name: Alpkit Filoment Hoody
description: 750 fill-power down hoody at a direct-sales price. Warm for the weight, thin outer fabric.

name: Rab Positron Pro Jacket
description: 800 fill-power belay jacket for standing still in the cold. Too warm to walk in.
